key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict complex, frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules quickly enough to replace expensive TD-DFT in screening workflows.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster molecular optical-property prediction for organic photovoltaic design and device-level simulations, supporting high-throughput materials discovery.
method: Input 3D molecular geometry and UV-vis spectral information to an equivariant GNN.
Predict the full complex-valued dynamic polarizability tensor across frequencies.
Validate predictions on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic molecules, then use them in downstream optical device simulations.
evidence_signal: The model reproduces main spectral features on both datasets and achieves strong agreement in device-level charge carrier generation rates with TD-DFT-based simulations ($R^2 = 0.94$).
watch_item: Performance depends on training data coverage and accurate molecular representations, so generalization to out-of-domain chemistries or simulation conditions should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
